item.title: Salmon company lashes out at own industry over ‘honesty’ on lice
item.description: A well known salmon farming company was told by Scottish Government inspectors to cut lice numbers at three of its sites in Sutherland. It responded by suggesting that other salmon farmers were failing to report lice numbers accurately.

item.title: Could AI misinformation sway the Scottish election?
item.description: Persuasive AI assistants, deepfakes and bots are now commonplace. But could they be used by bad actors to influence Scotland’s elections?

item.title: Books are being challenged in Scottish schools. Librarians fear a 'chilling effect' on freedom of speech
item.description: Dozens of complaints about reading material in school libraries have been received, with campaigners warning that "book bans" could increase.

item.title: CCA to be investigated over financial governance concerns
item.description: The Scottish charity regulator has announced it will investigate Glasgow's Centre for Contemporary Arts, which folded last month, due to concerns raised about its "historic financial management".

item.title: Claim John Swinney stayed at Peter Mandelson's residence is Mostly True
item.description: The first minister has been criticised online for staying with Mandelson on a trip to the US last year. We looked at the truth behind the claims.

item.title: Self-styled nightwatchmen patrol a Scottish village. Their leader is a Nazi
item.description: John Carroll says his nighttime rounds are protecting the community. Critics say his “abhorrent” views on Hitler, the Holocaust and race are incompatible with his adopted role.

item.title: Communities were promised a share of Scotland’s wind boom. Some are being sold short
item.description: More than 20 wind farms are failing to pay an agreed amount to locals. That could cost Scottish communities over £50m.

item.title: ‘Backroom’ lobbying on Coul Links golf plan under fire
item.description: Scottish ministers have been privately urged to back plans for a golf course on a coastal wildlife site. This has been condemned as “backdoor lobbying that tries to bypass the rules”.

item.title: Edinburgh Uni staff are losing their jobs. Their boss has two
item.description: Sir Peter Mathieson appears to have confirmed he is being paid for a board role at a university spin-off at the same time as many staff face uncertainty about their futures.

item.title: Does Sharia law have an influence in Scotland?
item.description: Sharia law is a contentious issue in the UK. Some question whether it is compatible with so-called British values while claiming it's a separate legal system operating parallel to UK laws. In our latest De-noiser, we look at the facts.
